title: ENIAC publicly unveiled
before: Large-scale calculation relied heavily on human computers, mechanical calculators, and specialized wartime machines with limited publicity and programmability models.
problem: Scientific and military computation needed much faster automatic electronic calculation.
change: ENIAC, designed by J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly, was unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania on 14 February 1946 (IEEE Computer Society timeline).
whyItMattered: It demonstrated large-scale electronic digital computation to a wide audience and influenced subsequent stored-program computer designs.
enabled: Accelerated investment and research in general-purpose electronic computers.
concreteExample: ENIAC performed ballistic trajectory calculations far faster than manual methods of the era.
caveat: Other wartime machines (e.g. Colossus) were operational earlier in specialized contexts. 'First computer' claims depend on definitions and were legally contested later.
